title: A Pod Off the Bow
coverImageAlt: Wildlife placeholder — real dolphin photography to come
excerpt: There were maybe sixty of them, riding the bow wave in relays for almost twenty minutes.
subtitle: Common dolphins show up in numbers in the channel between La Paz and Espíritu Santo, usually when you're not looking for them.
author: Thibault Poirson
body:
We see dolphins on most crossings, usually a handful, sometimes none. This particular pod was different, big enough that it took a while to realize how many animals were actually in the water around the boat.

They stayed with the bow wave the way dolphins do, peeling off and rejoining in relays, riding the pressure wave for a stretch and then dropping back to let the next group take a turn.

> Nobody ever really gets used to it. Twenty years of doing this and the crew was still out on the bow with everyone else.

![Placeholder — real photo under sail on the way back to Marina de La Paz to come](/assets/img/hero-premium.webp "Under sail on the way back to Marina de La Paz.")

The channel between La Paz and Espíritu Santo is one of the more reliable stretches for this, partly because of the current and partly because it's simply on the way to everywhere else we go.

We didn't plan the encounter and couldn't have. That's most of what wildlife-watching here actually is: putting the boat in the right general area and being ready when something shows up.
